# sysview

> sysview is a portable one-shot system stats viewer for Windows, Linux and macOS. A single static binary gives you a fast CLI overview, a live web dashboard, and Prometheus metrics — no runtime, no framework, no installer, no dependencies.

## About

- Current version: v0.3.0
- Platforms: Windows x86_64, Linux x86_64 (musl/glibc), macOS (universal)
- Binary size: about 1.8 MB (Windows) and 2.2 MB (Linux musl); 3.4 MB macOS universal
- Idle memory: about 2 MB RSS (roughly half of v0.2.0)
- Runtime: none (fully static); written in Rust
- License: MIT

## Commands

- `sysview` — full system overview (CPU, memory, disks, network, processes, sensors)
- `sysview sys|cpu|mem|procs|disks|net|vmstat|sensors` — one section; supports `--json` and `--watch`
- `sysview procs --top N --sort cpu|mem` - top processes by CPU or memory
- `sysview top` - full-screen live process monitor (`c`/`m`/`p`/`n` sort, `r` reverses, `+`/`-` resize, `q` quits; dependency-free terminal handling)
- `sysview export --format prometheus|csv [--section host|disks|procs|net]` - Prometheus text (the `/metrics` body) or CSV, rendered by the same code as the endpoint
- `sysview diff before.json [after.json]` - host-level comparison between snapshots or against the live host, with a reboot flag and `(new)`/`(gone)` mounts and interfaces (tolerates UTF-16 snapshots)
- `sysview cgroup` / `sysview gpu` - cgroup v2 limits this process actually runs under, and the GPUs the kernel reports (Linux)
- `sysview service install|uninstall|status [--system] [--print]` - register the dashboard with systemd, launchd or the Windows Task Scheduler; the token stays in an environment file rather than the process table, and `--print` shows the unit and commands without applying them
- `sysview serve --bind 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --token $SECRET` — live web dashboard and Prometheus `/metrics` on one port
- `sysview serve --interface wlan0 --kiosk` — bind to a named adapter's IPv4; start in kiosk mode
- `sysview serve --tls-cert fullchain.pem --tls-key privkey.pem` — terminate HTTPS in the binary (no reverse proxy, no new dependency)
- `sysview serve --alert-cpu 90 --alert-mem 90 --alert-disk '*:85' --alert-webhook https://ntfy.sh/topic` — POST when a threshold is crossed, repeats while hot, and once on recovery (ntfy / Slack / Discord / generic JSON)
- `sysview check --cpu 90 --mem 90 --disk 90 [--quiet|--json]` - one-shot threshold probe that exits non-zero on a breach (cron / CI)
- `sysview serve --history-file /var/lib/sysview/history.jsonl` - append one compact JSON line per sample and replay the tail on start, so the charts resume after a restart (trimmed to the newest window once it has grown past several); `GET /api/history` returns the rolling window alone
- `sysview serve --qr` - print a scannable QR code for the dashboard URL after the banner
- `sysview ports` / `sysview battery` — listening TCP sockets and battery state (Linux; also a dashboard panel)
- `sysview key add --label phone --expires 30d [--scope view]` — labelled keys with expiry and an `admin` or `view` scope (`key list`, `key rm`, `key expire`, `key scope`)
- `sysview update [--check|--force]` — self-update from GitHub Releases over HTTPS, verifying `SHA256SUMS` with no `git`/`curl`
- `systemctl status sysview` — deployed server service (systemd unit ships `Restart=always` and `MemoryMax=256M`)

## Dashboard

The embedded dashboard (served by `sysview serve`) includes a health score badge, disk "days until full" forecast, timeline markers (`M`), alert pulses when CPU/memory/swap run hot, a legacy retro theme, kiosk mode with an on-screen exit, a snapshot JSON download, a listening-ports & power panel (Linux), and a Settings panel for keys, interval, process cap, bind/interface/port and updates. A web app manifest makes it installable as a standalone app, and `/fleet` is a page (hosts kept in the browser's localStorage) for watching several hosts at once.

## Security

- `serve` binds `127.0.0.1` by default; use `--bind 0.0.0.0` to expose on your LAN
- `--token` protects every route (`/`, `/api/snapshot`, `/metrics`, `/health`, `/fleet`) with HTTP 401; labelled keys with optional expiry are supported and are scoped `admin` (full) or `view` (read-only — `403` on every state-changing route)
- Repeated bad tokens from one IP are throttled with `429`; a good token clears the counter
- `serve --tls-cert/--tls-key` terminates HTTPS in the binary (PKCS#8/PKCS#1/SEC1); `serve --cors` (opt-in) adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` to read routes so a fleet page on another origin can poll the host
- On servers, the token is stored root-only at `/etc/sysview/env`

## Metrics

Metrics are exposed as Prometheus text 0.0.4 gauges at `/metrics?token=...`. The full metric reference (with example values) is the metric table on the website.
